item.title: "Black Lodge" and "Bardo" — Fri Oct 30, 7:00 PM — Memorial Hall
item.description:
The night before Halloween, Memorial Hall transforms into something unsettling and mysterious.
Before the performance even begins, audiences are invited to enter BARDO, a haunting, liminal place between death and rebirth. Come dressed in your Halloween finest and venture through spaces rarely open to audiences. Eerie installations. Strange encounters. Unsettling imagery. Around every corner, the sense that something is waiting—and watching—just out of sight. North Carolina performers bring this dreamscape to life to create an experience that haunts long after the night is over.
The journey culminates with BLACK LODGE, a dark Lynchian goth-rock opera about a tormented writer trapped in the nightmarish Bardo, where he is forced to confront the darkest moment of his life again and again. item.title: JENNY BLAZING: CAROLINA, OR THEREABOUTS — Sat Oct 31, 1:00 PM — 5 Points Gallery
item.description: 5 Points Gallery is pleased to present Carolina, or Thereabouts, a new exhibition of mixed-media paintings by Featured Artist Jenny Blazing exploring the shifting nature of place through observation, memory, and imagination. Grounded in Blazing’s experiences of Carolina, the layered works draw from travel, accumulated visual memories, and unexpected connections that emerge as the paintings evolve to create landscapes that feel familiar without belonging to any single geography. Throughout the gallery, visitors can also enjoy work by our ten Triangle-based artists, offering a refreshing mix of painting, sculpture, fused glass, mixed media, and finely crafted furniture, with each artist bringing a distinct creative perspective. Join us for the Opening Reception on Friday, October 16, 2026, from 6–9 pm to meet the artist. Carolina, or Thereabouts runs from October 15 through November 14, 2026. item.title: Piano Masterclass: Awadagin Pratt — Sat Oct 31, 3:00 PM — East Duke 201 - Nelson Music Room
item.description:
Experience the artistry and insight of acclaimed pianist Awadagin Pratt in this engaging masterclass.
Praised by The Washington Post as "one of this country's most interesting and profound pianists," Pratt is among the most distinctive voices in American classical music. A winner of the Naumburg International Piano Competition and recipient of an Avery Fisher Career Grant, he has performed in solo recitals at Carnegie Hall and the Kennedy Center and appeared with leading orchestras across the country.
Through live coaching and musical exploration, Pratt will offer students and audience members a rare look into the interpretive choices, technique, and creative process behind a compelling performance.
This event is free and open to the public. All are welcome.
Source: Duke University

item.title: All Hallows' Eve Worship Service — Sat Oct 31, 10:30 PM — Duke Chapel
item.description:
All Hallows' Eve service is a festival in the church that recalls the faith and witness of those who have carried on and cherished the Christian faith throughout history. The service celebrates the Church's continuing communion with these men and women and memorializes the recently deceased. It comprises scripture readings, testimonies about saints, and anthems. The name of the service comes from its celebration on the night before All Saints' (or All Hallows') so it's "All Hallows' Eve," or "Halloween" (Halloween costumes are welcome at this service!).
All are welcome at this service. Free parking is available in the Bryan Center Garage at 125 Science Drive. ADA parking is available in the surface lot at the same address.
Source: Duke Arts, Duke University

item.description:

item.title: Jewish Studies Research Symposium — Sun Nov 1, 12:00 PM — Westbrook 0015
item.description:
The Sperling Center for Jewish Studies invites students, faculty, and community members to attend the 2026 Jewish Studies Annual Research Symposium on Sunday, November 1, 2026. This annual event showcases innovative research by Duke undergraduate and graduate students, as well as affiliated fellows, whose work engages Jewish history, culture, religion, literature, politics, and society across diverse geographical and historical contexts.
The symposium provides an opportunity for emerging scholars to present original research, share recent findings, and engage in interdisciplinary conversations with faculty, students, and members of the broader community. The symposium is free and open to the public. More information, including a detailed schedule and speaker bios, can be found at: https://jewishstudies.duke.edu/2026-sperl

item.title: Duke Arts Presents: Awadagin Pratt, America 250 — Sun Nov 1, 2:00 PM — Baldwin Auditorium
item.description:
Praised by The Washington Post as "one of this country's most interesting and profound pianists" Awadagin Pratt is one of the most distinctive artists in American classical music. Winner of the Naumburg International Piano Competition and recipient of an Avery Fisher Career Grant, Pratt has built a dynamic career with appearances ranging from solo recitals at Carnegie Hall and the Kennedy Center to collaborations with leading orchestras across the country.
His program, America 250, reflects on the breadth of American musical voices. Works by Florence Price, George Walker, and Nathaniel Dett appear alongside music by contemporary composers including Judd Greenstein and Fred Hersch. Pratt also performs his own arrangement of the spiritual Sometimes I Feel Like a Motherless Child, before closing with Brahms' monumental Variations and Fugue on a Theme of Handel.
Source: Duke University

item.description: Computational models of cardiac mechanics can serve as vital predictive tools to assist our understanding of cardiac pathologies. For example, we have developed a novel pipeline to convert pre-operative clinical images of the mitral valve into predictive patient specific models capable of accurately predicting the post-repair state. item.title: Chemistry Defense: Hung-Min Lin:"Dynamical Correlations and Transport in Superionic Argyrodites" — Mon Nov 2, 2:00 PM — None
item.description:
Superionic conductors are crystalline solids exhibiting liquid-like ionic diffusivity, making them promising for solid-state battery applications. Yet, the atomistic mechanisms governing their transport properties remain poorly understood. Here, I combine neutron scattering experiments with atomistic simulations to investigate the atomic structure and dynamics underlying ionic diffusion in argyrodite-type superionic materials.
I first investigate collective ionic hopping, long proposed as an origin of superionicity. Neutron scattering measurements on single-crystal Cu7PS6 reveal short-range dynamical correlations among diffusing ions, providing direct experimental evidence of collective hopping and resolving its spatiotemporal characteristics. Machine-learned molecular dynamics simulations reproduce these observations and provide complementary insights into the hopping mechanism. item.title: Critical Classicality: Book Talk and Poetry Reading — Mon Nov 2, 5:00 PM — Rubenstein Library Holsti-Anderson Family Assembly Room 153
item.description: In this talk, Kelly Nguyen shares the story behind her book, Critical Classicality in Vietnam and the Diaspora (Oxford University Press, 2026), and the poetry that emerged alongside it. The book traces how Vietnamese writers and thinkers have engaged with Greco-Roman antiquity, developing the concept of critical classicality: a way of confronting the classical tradition's complicity in colonialism and empire while also asking how those historically marginalized by that tradition might reclaim and remake it for their own liberatory purposes. But what happens when the histories we study refuse to stay on the page? Nguyen turns from scholarship to poetry, sharing select poems that were written alongside the book as a way of metabolizing the violence, silences, and trauma of the archives. Reimagining the Homeric Odyssey through the experiences of Vietnamese refugees, including her own and those of her parents, these poems put critical classicality into practice. Stitching Strength is a documentary film that captures the fight against ALS - a terminal disease that strips away the body's control - through lens of creativity, courage, and connection.
At its heart is Dr. Richard Bedlack, a neurologist whose bold fashion and bolder optimism set the tone for a radically different kind of care. But this isn't just his story. It's about the patients who refuse to be defined by their diagnosis, and the families who turn grief into art, music, and action.
This is not a story of surrender. It's a story of style, strength, and the power of believing in what's still possible. For Dr. Bedlack, fashion isn't just how you dress - it's an expression of joy. item.title: Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage — Thu Jan 28, 10:00 AM — Gregg Museum of Art & Design
item.description:
Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design presents a series of vignettes exploring spaces of dignity, belonging, safety, and imagination within Black communities across North Carolina. Featuring historical photographs, contemporary images, artworks from the Gregg Museum collection including a handmade guitar by Freeman Vines, and ephemera from community partners, the exhibition reflects on place, memory, creativity, and spiritual resilience across generations. Through stories of triumph and adversity, Community Stories honors the ways Black Americans have sustained and uplifted their communities through family, entrepreneurship, cultural expression, and soulful imagination, while inspiring future generations.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Introduction to Qualitative Interviewing — Thu Jan 28, 10:00 AM
item.description:
While there are ranges of ways to conduct research, interviewing is the most common form of data collection in qualitative research, with over half of qualitative studies relying on interview-based data. Interviews are valuable because they afford researchers opportunities to learn how people understand, interpret, and make meaning of their experiences through direct engagement. This introductory course provides practical skills for both designing and conducting semi-structured qualitative interviews (along with a brief overview of structured and unstructured interviewing).
Using course participants’ research interests, we will develop interview protocols, practice conducting effective interviews—with emphasis on active listening and asking productive follow-up questions. Participants will learn to formulate open-ended questions, organize interview questions around a research question, and use interview probes to invite elaboration, clarification, and reflection. item.title: Temple Theatre Presents: "One Noble Journey" — Thu Jan 28, 2:00 PM — Temple Theatre
item.description:
Temple Theatre is one of North Carolina's premier regional theatres, offering Broadway-quality productions in the heart of downtown Sanford.
After his family was torn apart and parceled out to various beneficiaries of the Louisa County, Virginia estate, Henry “Box” Brown, born into slavery, devised an ingenious escape plan – sealing himself in a wooden box for shipment to friends and freedom. One Noble Journey also recounts the daring and miraculous quest for freedom of Elizabeth Craft and her husband William.

item.title: EQUIP Spring Check-in — Thu Jan 28, 5:30 PM — Witherspoon Student Center
item.description:
Join the African American Cultural Center (AACC) for the EQUIP spring check-in and to learn how this year-long initiative can help you create the college experience you want in and outside of the classroom. EQUIP stands for Empower, Question, Understand, Initiate and Partner. The initiative is designed to help first-year students:
Empower themselves to create the college experience they wantQuestion everything to build habits for life-long learningUnderstand themselves and what they need to be successfulInitiate action and be proactive to find resourcesPartner with others to build a network of care and communityAs an EQUIP participant, you will:
Engage in monthly check-ins with a dedicated staff memberAttend learning labs and AACC signature eventsWork with an embedded AACC counselorAttend EQUIP special programsDevelop skills in self-awareness, resilience and help-seekingContact Andaiye Qaasim, assistant director of the AACC, at aaqaasim@ncsu.edu if you have questions.
